title: Regression Firebreak + A/B Compare Onboarding - LedgerCo

Customer is evaluating a pilot (500k calls/month) and wants clarity on alert noise, private deployment constraints, and data retention for logs.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (LedgerCo Head of ML), Owen (Platform), Dana (Sec Ops)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone — thanks for carving time. This is Maya from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. with me is Carlos, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya: Good, thanks. we've got a tight agenda, we want to see how you detect regressions and do clean A/B compares without getting spammy alerts.
[00:16] Owen: and also we need to understand the network setup — VPC, private log retention stuff.
[00:22] Dana: SOC2 and KMS questions — quick ones up front if possible.
[00:27] Carlos: Great. we'll do a short Console walkthrough then switch into the API and Optimize recommendations — focus on prompt sets, thresholds, and a splitbench A/B flow.
[00:36] Maya: Quick qualification — you're planning a pilot volume around 500k inference calls a month?
[00:41] Priya: Roughly, yes. Some spikey times around payroll cutoffs. latency matters but cost is also a hard constraint — we can't justify premium on every route.
[00:50] Carlos: Understood. Redwood supports routing policies so you can route important traffic to lower-latency dedicated pools and overflow to cheaper hosted variants. For monitoring, we'll show per-route token cost and quality metrics so you can measure the tradeoff.
[01:05] [Screen share starts: Redwood Console — home dashboard]
[01:12] Carlos: Here is the Console — you'll see Workspaces. I'm opening LedgerCo demo workspace we pre-populated. First tab is Prompt Sets. You can create a set with examples and expected outputs, label "success criteria", and upload human judgments.
[01:26] Priya: When you say "success criteria" can that be a multi-field check? e.g., entity extraction + tone score?
[01:33] Carlos: Yes, you can compose metrics. We have built-in matchers for exact vs. fuzzy, regex for extraction, and a small sentiment model for tone. You can also plug in your own scorer via webhook.
[01:44] Dana: Are those scoring webhooks executed inside our VPC or outbound to Redwood-managed infra?
[01:50] Carlos: If you're on Private deployment we can host scoring inside your VPC; for Hosted, webhooks go out to your endpoint over TLS. We support SAML SSO and KMS integrations for keying.
[02:02] [00:02:02] Maya: Jumping to regression alerts — you define a baseline window and a threshold. For example, if accuracy drops by 3% relative to baseline over N samples, fire an alert.
[02:14] Priya: Is the baseline rolling or fixed? we often see seasonal shifts.
[02:19] Carlos: Both. You can pick fixed baseline (e.g., last week's evaluation set) or rolling with smoothing. We also have an adaptive noise filter — it'll learn expected variance to avoid flapping.
[02:31] Owen: What's the SLO for detection latency? we prefer near-real-time for high-severity ops.
[02:36] Carlos: Alerts are evented at ingestion — typically within 30s for streaming telemetry; for batch re-evals it's when the job completes.
[02:44] Priya: Can we tune alert routing? We don't want infra paged for small policy drifts.
[02:50] Carlos: Yes — you can set severity levels and route to different Slack channels, PagerDuty, or create silent tickets in Jira.
[03:00] [03:00] Carlos: Now A/B compares — we call it splitbench. You create two buckets, pin model version A vs B, define traffic split and metrics, and then run playback on historical prompts to estimate lift.
[03:15] Priya: Do you support KV cache differences? our infra uses a caching layer that impacts outputs for longer context sessions.
[03:23] Carlos: Good point — playback can be run in two modes: stateless (no KV) or session-accurate (replay with KV priming). The session mode requires logs of KV snapshots; if you can't provide those we'll approximate and flag uncertainty.
[03:36] [04:00] Maya: Quick interruption — I heard you mention quantization earlier in the RFP, Priya — are you expecting recommendations?
[04:06] Priya: Yeah, cost/perf tradeoffs. we want to know when to push to a quantized variant.
[04:10] Carlos: Redwood Optimize suggests quant levels per route by simulating latency and comparing quality drop on your prompt set. It will suggest a conservative quant option with estimated token-cost savings.
[04:22] Dana: Security — audit logs retention. how long do you keep raw prompt + response data in Hosted?
[04:28] Maya: Hosted stores up to 90 days by default; longer retention is an add-on. Private installs can be configured to your data retention policy and can integrate with your archival S3. All stored content can be encrypted via customer KMS.
[04:40] Dana: And redaction? PII controls?
[04:43] Carlos: You can plug in pre-ingest scrubbing rules in the Console or run redaction in the SDK. We also support tokenization to limit raw storage.
[04:52] [05:00] [Screen: Splitbench configuration page]
[05:05] Carlos: Here's a sample run: Model A is open-7b-vanilla, Model B is open-7b-quantized. We run 10k prompts, compute metrics: exact match, recall, hallucination rate, and an aggregate quality score. This UI shows uplift and CI bands.
[05:22] Priya: How do you compute hallucination? that's a fuzzy one.
[05:26] Carlos: We use reference-based checks plus semantic similarity thresholds; for certain tasks we recommend manual annotation for final gating. There's also a "human-in-the-loop" workflow that surfaces low-confidence outputs for annotation.
[05:38] Owen: If we run a live A/B with 10% traffic to B, can we auto-fallback if B drifts?
[05:45] Carlos: Yes — built-in rollback policies. You can set auto-fallback rules on latency or quality metrics. If B's error rate exceeds X for Y minutes, traffic is switched back.
[05:55] Priya: Show me the alert noise controls — this is where we've had trouble before.
[06:00] [06:00] Carlos: In Alert config, you can set min sample count, effect size, p-value thresholds, and a suppress window. We also provide a dry-run mode showing the alerts that would have fired historically.
[06:15] Maya: We'll attach a sample suppress config and the dry-run output to the pilot folder.
[06:20] [07:00] [Short demo of API call example]
[07:05] Carlos: If you prefer code, here's the API call to submit a prompt-set evaluation and start a splitbench job. (reads snippet) "POST /v1/evals/splitbench" — payload includes prompt_set_id, model_versions, rollout_pct, metrics.
[07:22] Priya: Any rate limits? we plan bursts up to 200 RPS for payroll windows.
[07:27] Carlos: For Hosted, default burst policy is 100 RPS per route; Dedicated can support sustained high RPS and we can provision autoscaling. For pilot we recommend a dedicated small pool for the critical path.
[07:40] Dana: For Private, is full traffic internal or does Redwood control-plane need callbacks?
[07:46] Carlos: With Private, control plane calls back over a customer-managed tunnel for telemetry, but data plane remains in your VPC. You can also run fully air-gapped with an on-prem bundle if required.
[07:57] [08:00] Priya: Let's talk expected false positive rate — you mentioned adaptive filters, but we need hard numbers.
[08:04] Carlos: Hard numbers vary by task. For extraction tasks we've seen FP under 2% with a min-sample of 500 and smoothing enabled; for generative summarization it's higher. We'll run your prompts through a baseline to give concrete numbers.
[08:18] Priya: ok, that baseline will help.
[08:21] Maya: Quick Q: who in your team will be the technical lead for the pilot?
[08:25] Priya: Owen for infra and Dana for security, I'll own success criteria.
[08:30] [09:00] [Questions from Dana]
[09:04] Dana: Can we get a SOC2 report and do you have ISO?
[09:08] Maya: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II; ISO is in our roadmap — I'll send the cert and the SOC report after the call.
[09:15] Dana: And do you support customer KMS with HSM-backed keys?
[09:19] Carlos: We integrate with common KMS providers; HSM-backed keys supported on Private installs.
[09:24] [10:00] [Walkthrough: alert dry-run output — shows several historical alerts but suppressed due to low sample size]
[10:11] Priya: This suppression looks useful. can you export the raw events?
[10:15] Carlos: Yes, you can export to CSV or stream to your SIEM via our Audit API.
[10:22] Owen: What's the storage cost for logs?
[10:26] Maya: For Hosted there's a per-GB retention fee; we'll include estimates in the pricing doc. Private is negotiated.
[10:35] [12:00] Maya: Alright, recap. We'll provision a demo workspace, Carlos will drop the splitbench sample and scripts, and I'll send the SOW.
[12:12] Priya: Timeline wise, we want pilot kickoff in the last week of July.
[12:16] Owen: We'll share anonymized prompts by Monday.
[12:20] Dana: And I'll need the SOC2 and data flow diagram.
[12:24] Maya: Noted.
[12:27] [13:00] Closing chatter — small talk and schedule confirmations.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription mislabels some model names (e.g., "open-7b" as "open7 b") and occasionally transposes Redwood product names ("Redwood Optimize" -> "Redwood Opera tives"). There are small gaps where speakers overlap.

End of transcript.
